items.title: Ancient Egypt
items.summary: Ancient Egypt was a society that began around 3150 BCE and lasted until 30 BCE, when it was invaded by the Romans.

items.title: Great Pyramid of Giza
items.summary: The Great Pyramid of Giza is a huge pyramid built by the Ancient Egyptians over 4,500 years ago. It stands 18.4 km from Cairo, Egypt.

items.title: Sphinx
items.summary: A sphinx (Boeotian: φίξ [pʰíːks], plural sphinxes or sphinges) is a mythical creature with the head of a human, the body of a lion, and the wings of an eagle.

items.title: Ancient Greece
items.summary: Ancient Greek civilization, also commonly called Ancient Greece, was a large area, mostly along the northeast shore of the Mediterranean Sea, where people spoke the Greek language. The area was much larger than today's country of Greece.

items.title: Roman Empire
items.summary: The Roman Empire ruled the Mediterranean and much of Europe, Western Asia and North Africa. The Romans conquered most of this during the Republic, and it was ruled by emperors following Octavian's assumption of effective sole rule in 27 BC.

items.title: Julius Caesar
items.summary: Gaius Julius Caesar (12 July 100 BC – 15 March 44 BC) was a military commander, politician and author at the end of the Roman Republic.

items.title: Alexander the Great
items.summary: Alexander the Great was Alexander III of Macedonia 20/21 July 356 BC – 10/11 June 323 BC). He was king of the ancient kingdom of Macedonia from 336 BC until his death in 323 BC.

items.title: Tutankhamun
items.summary: Tutankhamun (Tutankhaten, Tutankhamun) was an Egyptian Pharaoh of the 18th dynasty (royal family) during New Kingdom. He reigned from when he was nine years old (1334 BC) to when he died (1324 BC).

items.title: Great Wall of China
items.summary: The Great Wall of China (traditional Chinese: 萬里長城; simplified Chinese: 万里长城; pinyin: Wànlǐ Chángchéng, literally "ten thousand li long wall") is a series of fortifications in China.

items.title: Colosseum
items.summary: The Colosseum, also known as the Flavian Amphitheatre, is a large artefact or structure in the city of Rome. The construction of the Colosseum started around 70–72 AD and was finished in 80 AD.

items.title: Stonehenge
items.summary: Stonehenge is a prehistoric World Heritage Site of megaliths. It is eight miles (13 kilometres) north of Salisbury in Wiltshire, England.

items.title: Mayan civilization
items.summary: The Maya civilization was a pre-Colombian Central American civilization from around 2000 BC to 1698 CE.

items.title: Aztecs
items.summary: The Aztecs were Native American people who lived in Mesoamerica. They ruled the Aztec Empire from the 14th century to the 16th century.

items.title: Inca Empire
items.summary: The Inca were a pre-Columbian country and empire in the Andes of South America. The word 'Inca' can also mean the emperor or king of the Inca people.

items.title: Machu Picchu
items.summary: Machu Picchu is a pre-Columbian 15th-century Inca site in Peru, in South America.

items.title: Vikings
items.summary: The Vikings were Scandinavian people from Northern Europe who were known as great seamen and warriors. The Scandinavian countries include Norway, Sweden and Denmark.

items.title: Middle Ages
items.summary: The Middle Ages were a period of about 1000 years in European history. They took place between the end of the Western Roman Empire in 476 CE when Romulus Augustulus was deposed, and the beginning of the Renaissance around 1400 - 1500 CE.

items.title: Renaissance
items.summary: The Renaissance is a period in European history that followed the Middle Ages and ended in the 17th century. Renaissance is a French word for “cultural rebirth.”

items.title: Industrial Revolution
items.summary: The Industrial Revolution is the name of the time when there was a big change in the way things were made. Instead of things being hand-made in small workshops, they were made more cheaply in large quantities by machines in factories.

items.title: Silk Road
items.summary: The Silk Road was a group of trade routes across Asia that connected China with the Mediterranean region. It allowed Chinese traders to exchange things with Middle Eastern and Mediterranean traders.

items.title: Mali Empire
items.summary: The Mali Empire was a West African realm from 1267 to 1641. The Mandinka people lived there they still are in some parts of Africa today.

items.title: Kingdom of Aksum
items.summary: The Kingdom of Aksum (Ge'ez: መንግስቲ ኣኽሱም), also known as the Kingdom of Axum or the Aksumite Empire, was an ancient kingdom centered in what is now Eritrea and the Tigray Region of northern Ethiopia.

items.title: Great Zimbabwe
items.summary: Great Zimbabwe is a ruined city in the southeastern hills of Zimbabwe. It was a royal city for the Zimbabwean monarch.

items.title: Pompeii
items.summary: Pompeii was an ancient city that was buried by Mount Vesuvius. It is currently a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

items.title: Rosetta Stone
items.summary: The Rosetta Stone is a stone with writing carved into it. There are 3 types of writing on the Rosetta stone; Greek, Egyptian, and another form of Egyptian writing.

items.title: Colossus of Rhodes
items.summary: The Colossus of Rhodes was a huge statue of the Greek god, Helios built on the Greek island of Rhodes by Chares of Lindos (a student of Lysippos) between 294 and 282 BC.

items.title: Lighthouse of Alexandria
items.summary: The Lighthouse of Alexandria, or the Pharos, was a tall tower built between 285 and 247 BCE. It was built on the island of Pharos in Alexandria, Egypt to serve as a lighthouse for sailors.

items.title: Hanging Gardens of Babylon
items.summary: The Hanging Gardens of Babylon, and the walls of Babylon (near present-day Al Hillah in Iraq) were one of the Seven Wonders of the World. They were built by Nebuchadnezzar II around 600 BC.

items.title: Temple of Artemis
items.summary: The Temple of Artemis (Greek: Ἀρτεμίσιον or Latin: Artemisium), was a temple dedicated to the goddess Artemis. It was also known as the Temple of Diana (Diana was a Roman goddess).

items.title: Wonders of the World
items.summary: The Seven Wonders of the World (or the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World) is a widely-known list of seven great buildings or structures from the classical time period.
